messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing a spike of NVIDIA Xid 48 and 79 across the a10-embedder pool in us-east-2 between 02:12–02:28 UTC. Roughly ~40 cards hit errors, seems concentrated on small-batch embedder and low-temp decode tails. Can we triage?
infra-bot: Alert: 40 Xid events in 16m on cluster a10-embedder-us-east-2. Incident created: INC-1234. Link: https://redwood/incident/INC-1234 :rotating_light:
sam: Which tenants / job ids? Any obvious op types or batch sizes?
maria: Most are from tenant cohorts "search-embed" and "semantic-ranking" — batch sizes 1–2, seq len ~512. I grepped the edge logs for the Xid lines: ```[2026-03-17T02:14:11Z] gpu0 Xid 48 decode_timeout kernel: module=nvdec pid=2743 job=embed-9a3f
[2026-03-17T02:14:35Z] gpu3 Xid 79 p2p_fault pid=3312 job=rank-4c1b
[2026-03-17T02:15:02Z] gpu0 Xid 48 decode_timeout pid=2765 job=embed-9a3f
```
alex: Do ECC counters move? temps? nvlink/pcie errors? Can you run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,POWER,TEMP` on the affected GPUs and paste outputs. Also include driver version `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` — sometimes NIC/PCIe retries coincide with Xid 79.
jin: Noted a scheduling pattern — the spike aligns with an autoscale event at 02:15 where ~120 workers came up and many hit cold KV cache lookups. That KV thrash increases small decode loops and memory pressure.
maria: Pulled telemetry from the affected hosts. ECC L1/L2 counters are flat, but device decode timeout counters and TLB-related timeouts increased. NIC rx_err counters show a small bump on the same hosts. Snippet: ```GPU=0 TEMP=68C POWER=220W ECC=0/0 TLB_miss=1250 decode_timeouts=6 NIC_rx_err=4```
sam: Might be driver/firmware interplay — what driver are we on? I remember a regression around Xid79 with 525.x fixed in 530.x. Can you check `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv`?
alex: Proposal: 1) isolate small-batch workload to a separate pool for 6h (so we can observe without impacting high-priority traffic) 2) soft-drain the top-10 hot cards, run `nvidia-bug-report.sh` + stress testing, collect `dmesg`/kernel logs 3) if reproducible, escalate for hardware replacement and firmware/driver escalation. Example drain command: `fleetctl soft-drain gpunode-061 --grace 300`
ops-runner: Scheduling soft-drain for nodes gpunode-061..070 starting in +10m. Note: us-east-2 commit is ~78% — we'll shift best-effort low-priority jobs to us-west-1 to keep SLA. :construction:
maria: 👍 starting data collection and will upload bug reports to INC-1234. I'll attach `nvidia-bug-report` outputs and edge logs.
infra-bot: Incident INC-1234 updated. Assigned: sam, alex. Priority: P2. :bell:
sam: Quick repro attempt — ran `stress-ng --gpu 1` and a small decode loop locally against a cached model, could not reproduce; suggests it's workload + driver + cluster-level event (autoscale / NIC) rather than purely HW failure.
maria: Next steps: collect full bug reports from affected nodes, try a firmware driver bump/downgrade test on one canary node, and check for kernel NMI/watchdog logs during the window. I'll post updates to INC-1234 and loop in HW support if we get a repeat.
alex: Also add task to correlate Xid events to autoscale timestamps and NIC interrupt spikes (pcie errors). If we see strong co-occurrence, ops can introduce jitter in worker startup to avoid thundering herd.
maria: Good call. Will also pin the small-batch embedder tenants to a new pool and run for 6h. If errors persist on pinned cards we soft-replace.
ops-runner: Done — pool pinned, soft-drains scheduled. Will monitor token throughput and cost delta.
maria: Thanks all — I'll update once we have bug-report archives attached. :eyes:
